Confusable pairs among the DUI and license-loss rules, followed by continuation facts that did not fit part C; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
Implied consent is about refusing a test, which brings revocation for refusal, while illegal per se is about the test result itself, which brings revocation at .08% or with any detectable controlled substance. [A01]
Why it matters: group DUI law; confusable implied consent versus illegal per se.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
The adult per se level is .08% alcohol concentration, while drivers under 21 face action starting at .02%. [A01]
Why it matters: group DUI law; confusable adult versus under-21 limits.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
The handbook reports that in 2016 alcohol-related crashes were a factor in over 31% of Nevada roadway deaths, and that from 2012 to 2015 alcohol and drugs contributed to 4,651 injury crashes in the state. [A01]
Why it matters: group DUI statistics; historical figures; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A01
An administrative penalty is the DMV's action and stands regardless of the court's findings, while a criminal penalty is imposed by the court. [A01]
Why it matters: group DUI law; confusable administrative versus criminal.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A02
A first DUI carries jail of two days up to six months, with 48 to 96 hours of community service as the alternative, while a second DUI within 7 years brings 10 days to 6 months plus 100 to 200 hours of community service. [A02]
Why it matters: group DUI penalties; confusable first versus second offense.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A02
Fines rise with each DUI: $400 to $1,000 for a first, $750 to $1,000 for a second within 7 years, and $2,000 to $5,000 for a later offense or one causing death or serious injury. [A02]
Why it matters: group DUI penalties; confusable fine ranges.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A02
A second DUI within 7 years can bring possible registration suspension and an order for treatment or clinical supervision by a treatment facility for up to one year. [A02]
Why it matters: group DUI penalties; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A02
For commercial driver license holders, any detectable alcohol can affect the driving privilege, and DUI penalties are harsher, including lifetime disqualification from commercial driving. [A02]
Why it matters: group DUI penalties; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A02
With a first DUI conviction, the judge may count time already served under the administrative revocation toward the minimum 185-day criminal revocation. [A02]
Why it matters: group DUI penalties; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A03
Young drivers face the same 185-day revocation period and the same reinstatement options, including ignition interlock, as drivers over the age of 18. [A03]
Why it matters: group young drivers; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A03
Following too closely, using two lanes, drifting off the road or straight through turn lanes, and swerving to correct course are also listed as clues to an impaired driver. [A03]
Why it matters: group impairment clues; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A03
The handbook notes that in 2019, 129 people died in alcohol-related crashes in Nevada, 42 percent of all traffic deaths. [A03]
Why it matters: group DUI statistics; historical figures; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A04
Licenses lost to suspension or revocation require reapplying, documents, any other requirements and fees, and license issuance may be delayed for some juvenile offenses. [A04]
Why it matters: group reinstatement; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A04
The street racing and trick driving ground covers both taking part in and organizing an unauthorized speed contest or trick display, whether on a public highway or on premises the public can access. [A04]
Why it matters: group license loss; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0082]
